chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Hilal from Uqbah ibn Khalid from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) issued a ruling regarding the watering of palm trees by means of the stream (sail): the upper [palm trees] drink before the lower [ones], and the water is lowered to the level of the ankles, then the water is released to the lower [ones], and the one next to them [in turn] is like that, until the walls [of the channels] are finished and the water is exhausted.

key_terms.السَّيْل: A stream or channel used for irrigation, often referring to a specific method of watering where water flows through channels.
key_terms.الْأَعْلَى: The upper [palm trees], referring to those located at the higher end of the water source.
key_terms.الْحَوَائِط: The walls or banks of the irrigation channels, referring to the boundaries of the watered area.
key_terms.الْكَعْبَيْنِ: The ankles, indicating the depth to which water is lowered or allowed to settle before moving to the next section.

ai.seo_question: How is water distributed among neighbors for watering palm trees according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, establishes the customary practice ('urf) of water distribution in agrarian societies, prioritizing upstream owners to ensure equitable access before the resource is depleted. It reflects the Shia juristic principle of preventing harm ('darar) and maintaining social harmony by codifying a clear, sequential order for resource allocation. The ruling underscores the importance of customary practice in Islamic law, where established local norms are validated by the Imams as binding legal precedents.
